In 1 day, this Gucci x Crocs concept gained 100,000s of views, 2,000+ Saves and hundreds of questions:

"how to make this" and "where to find the prompts?"

The answer is: here and now. Scroll down and grab all the assets in this Article 👇

THE IDEA: image-to-engine

When I was a kid, I loved big ideas. As I grew up, I realized it is impossible to bring all of my ideas to life . My life just won't have enough years for that...

Real mastery takes years to hone, and vision takes decades to mature. That was sad to accept. So, I played small.

But in 2026, everything has changed with AI.

I thought once: “What if I could take an image I love and → extract the main part that hooked me → transform it into a completely different idea?”

I ran a test - and it worked! Let me show you how: Repeat the steps below 👇

I built a ready to use pipeline with all the prompts & logic for you:

it's in my LTX project in the end of this Article.

Scroll down and grab it now - for free.

4 TOOLS YOU NEED

  1. Pinterest/Behance- for visual inspo & references,
  2. ChatGPT - to turn your image into a base brand board,
  3. LTX Flows - to grab my base pipeline + scale your campaigns.
  4. Prompts below - to make it all work and look great.

Scroll down, grab all the prompts and FREE GIFTS, waiting for you at the end of the article. Fully prepared LTX project link is there, too.

My creative direction logic

Creative direction logic

here’s exactly how I thought as CD:

  1. Found an image that hooked me with its vibe
  2. Extracted its creative system (prompt below)
  3. Imagined luxury fashion × streetwear tension
  4. Built a vision around it (with ChatGPT)
  5. Made product the hero
  6. Built consistent visual language across all assets

This thinking framework helps you create stronger design systems, easier.

💡I beg you to learn more about traditional CD & creative marketing frameworks - your skill with skyrocket with AI then.

Below are all the prompts I used, in the exact order.

PROMPT 1. Reference deconstruction

Step 0: we extract the whole style from the reference image - and turn it into a Brandboard - the guiderails for GPT2 to then build another concept on top of it.

Upload your image in LTX Flows + add this prompt in the prompt node 👇

PROMPT:

You are a world-class Creative Director and Brand Designer working at a top-tier agency.

Using the provided reference image as the source of truth, create a clean 4:3 visual brand board.

Do NOT copy the reference directly. Extract and rebuild its underlying creative system:

* core idea and creative tension
* color and material language
* typography direction
* image and composition logic
* signature visual device
* layout/grid system
* scalable campaign applications

The output must be a polished visual brand board, not a text-heavy document.

Design direction:

* premium editorial layout
* clear modular grid
* strong hero visual area
* limited, readable labels only
* large visual tiles
* minimal micro-copy
* no overcrowding
* no overlapping text on active backgrounds
* clean margins and consistent spacing

The board should feel like a professional agency campaign direction slide: visual, structured, immediately understandable, and ready to use as the foundation for a full brand campaign.

Your first steps in Flows - this is how you set up production grade design pipelines in simple steps.

Access Flows:

  1. go to
    https://amirmushich.link/AMIR-LTX
  2. click "generate images" - and you'll get to the Gen Space
  3. in Gen Space, in the top center, you'll find the Flows tab

PROMPT 2. Building your concept

Let's integrate OUR brand into the creative flow & logic.

> AI takes the system from our previous step, > applies it to our new brand - using the prompt below:

In the prompt below, I changed [INSERT ANY BRAND HERE] to [GUCCI x CROCS]

On this stage, you start owning the aesthetics & creative logic

PROMPT:

recreate the whole campaign document for [INSERT ANY BRAND HERE] 
imaginary collab campaign, 
using the source image I provided as a material & vibe reference, 
but rebuild it completely according to new brands' visual aesthetic
and brand guidelines, 
be especially careful with brands' fonts consistency and accuracy

PROMPT 3. Creating assets

Now, we'll create a set of branded visual assets.

  • Posts,
  • banners,
  • mockups,
  • close-ups,
  • details

we want to see the bigger picture and lock in the direction. Once you good with it, we are ready to move on. We will create the actual assets later

PROMPT:

Now create me a moodboard of actual visual assets for this campaign:
* digital banners, 
* social media banners & posts, 
* ad materials, 
* aesthetical assets 
etc

avoid overlapping text layers over active backgrounds 

make 30% less images, but make them tighter 
and looking more like a bento grid

NOTE:

GPT-v2 can overlap text on models' faces - which looks horrible. Find the "patch prompt" to fix this in the bonus LTX Project below 👇

More prompts & the working pipeline - in my LTX Project below

PROMPT 4. Lock the vision

Once you feel the direction feels right, capture it in the Brief Slide.

That is useful for you, for the AI, and for a potential client - because everyone now has the clear concept & vision.

I personally learn a lot from these slides - from creative twists to foundational insights about branding, marketing, and design.

The prompt is simple but powerful 👇

A simple prompt turns your direction into the vision

PROMPT:

now create me a slide with this campaign's 
* brief, 
* idea 
* and goals

PROMPT 5. Key visuals

Once our strategy and design vision finalized, it's time to create Key Visuals (KV).

A key visual is the main visual carrier of the campaign. It sets the mood, idea, color, composition, and first impression.

KVs help the brand make the strategy look fresh, relevant, and sales‑driven every single time.

Let’s create them - prompt below 👇

PROMPT:

now create a clean image slide with 
a photo scene of campaign-relevant characters 
positioned in  a campaign-relevant surrounding 
with campaign slogan positioned on top of the photograph 
in a fashion-magazine typography design style and level

act as a world class art director 
presenting the campaign with a single visual slide:
the key visual that deserves to be on the first page of 
Forbes or Esquire magazines

I don't need an overwhelmed tech slide, 
I need a cover art for the whole campaign
